I have everything needed. Here is my report.

## Summary

**Redis is NOT used anywhere in this repository.** The caching layer is a **custom, in-memory, TTL-based cache** implemented in Go. There is no Redis, ioredis, or any external cache store. (The `createClient` hits in the frontend are Connect-RPC clients, unrelated to caching. `golang-lru/v2` appears in `/bench/repo/go.sum` but is NOT imported by any Go source file — it is an unused/indirect dependency.)

---

## 1. Redis usage

None. No `redis`, `ioredis`, or Redis client anywhere in the Go backend or the web frontend. No `go-redis`, no connection strings, no config.

---

## 2. Where the cache layer is implemented and configured

### The cache implementation (the actual mechanism)
`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` — a custom thread-safe in-memory cache backed by `sync.Map`, with per-item TTL expiration, a background cleanup goroutine, a max-items cap, and rough size estimation.

Key points:
- `Cache` struct (lines 66-73) uses `sync.Map` + an atomic item counter.
- Each `item` (lines 34-39) stores `value`, `expiration time.Time`, and `size`.
- `Config` (lines 41-54): `DefaultTTL`, `CleanupInterval`, `MaxItems`, `OnEviction`.
- `DefaultConfig()` (lines 56-64): `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`.
- `Set` (lines 92-95) applies `c.config.DefaultTTL`; `SetWithTTL` (lines 97-120) allows a custom TTL.
- `Get` (lines 122-147) lazily evicts expired entries; `cleanupLoop`/`cleanup` (lines 199-250) periodically purge expired items; `cleanupOldest` (lines 252-313) evicts ~20% when over `MaxItems`.

### Where it is configured/wired
`/bench/repo/store/store.go`:
- Lines 27-29: three cache instances on the `Store` struct — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`.
- Lines 40-45: the `cacheConfig` used for all three:
  ```go
  cacheConfig := cache.Config{
      DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
      CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
      MaxItems:        1000,
      OnEviction:      nil,
  }
  ```
- Lines 51-53: all three caches created via `cache.New(cacheConfig)`.
- Lines 74-76: caches closed (cleanup goroutines stopped) on `Store.Close()`.

### Cache consumers
- Users: `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (Set at lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167; Get at line 150; key builder `userCacheKey` lines 88-90).
- User settings: `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` (lines 59, 78, 86, 106, 122); key builder `getUserSettingCacheKey` in `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` line 7.
- Instance settings: `/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go` (line 146 Get; `cacheInstanceSetting` at line 166 → Set at line 170).
- Cache invalidation on user delete: `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` lines 39-45.

### Other, unrelated caching in the repo (for completeness)
- HTTP `Cache-Control` headers for the frontend static server: `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go` lines 24-26 and 94-104 (HTML: `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`; static assets: `public, max-age=3600`; hashed assets: `public, max-age=3600, immutable`).
- On-disk derived-file caches for attachments: `/bench/repo/store/attachment.go` lines 75-76 (`.thumbnail_cache`, `.motion_cache`).
- Frontend editor draft cache (localStorage, not entity caching): `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/cacheService.ts`.

---

## 3. TTL applied to "user" entries specifically

**There is NO user-specific TTL.** User entries are cached with the shared default TTL only.

- Every user write path calls plain `s.userCache.Set(...)` (`/bench/repo/store/user.go` lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167), and `Set` applies `c.config.DefaultTTL` (`cache.go` line 94).
- The `userCache` is constructed with the same `cacheConfig` as the other caches (`store.go` lines 40-45, 52), so its `DefaultTTL` is **10 minutes**, with cleanup every 5 minutes and a 1000-item cap.
- `SetWithTTL` (custom per-entry TTL) is **never called on the user cache** — the only non-test call site of `SetWithTTL` is internally from `Set` in `cache.go` line 94. It is otherwise used only in `cache_test.go`.

So: users are cached in-memory for a default 10-minute TTL, identical to instance settings and user settings; there is no distinct/override TTL for user entries.
